status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026, checked by the translation workers, and deployed to earthfluent.com on 13 November 2026. Simplified characters, as the rest of the course. The course stores no pinyin, so where the sound is the lesson, the pinyin is in the description.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Four Tones, Part 1
lessons.description: One sound, four words: in Chinese the tone is part of the word. Listen to mā (high and level), má (rising), mǎ (dipping), and mà (falling).

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Four Tones, Part 2
lessons.description: Change the tone and you change the word. Hear mǎi against mài, and tāng against táng.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Characters That Are Pictures, Part 1
lessons.description: The oldest characters began as drawings. Look for the walking legs in 人, the three peaks in 山, the open mouth in 口, and the trunk and branches in 木.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Characters Built from Parts, Part 1
lessons.description: Most characters are built from simpler ones. Woman 女 and child 子 side by side make good, 好. Sun 日 and moon 月 make bright, 明.

lessons.title: Patterns - The Verb Never Changes, Part 1
lessons.description: A Chinese verb never changes. Only the word in front says who is going: 我, 你, 她, 我们. Spot what stays the same.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One Person, Part 1
lessons.description: Add 们 after a word for a person and it means more than one: 我 is I, and 我们 is we.

lessons.title: Patterns - Already Done, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb itself has no past. Put 了 after it to say the thing is done.

lessons.title: Patterns - Counting Words, Part 1
lessons.description: Between a number and a thing goes a counting word, and different kinds of thing take different ones: 个 for people, 本 for books, 只 for animals, 辆 for vehicles.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: Add 吗 to the end of a statement and it becomes a question. Nothing else moves.
words: This is the bus to Beijing.
这是去北京的公共汽车。
Is this the bus to Beijing?
这是去北京的公共汽车吗？

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: To say something is not so, put 不 in front of the verb. Nothing else in the sentence changes. One everyday verb is different: 有, to have, takes 没, so I do not have a car is 我没有车.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - When Comes Before the Verb, Part 1
lessons.description: English puts the time at the end: I go tomorrow. Chinese puts it before the verb: I tomorrow go.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come First, Part 1
lessons.description: As in English, the describing word comes before the thing it describes.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb 去, to go, at work in whole sentences. It is the same 去 every time, whoever is going.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. The answer drops 吗, and a no adds 不.
words: No, I do not speak English.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: Where English says the house is big, Chinese says the house very big: 很 stands where English puts is.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways. The verb 去 never changes: the day word says when, with 了 for what is done, and sometimes 要 for what is still to come.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
I am going to the market today.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
I am going to go tomorrow.
